full_text_en:
Bank of China et al. (Five Banks) v. Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd. — Enforcement of Arbitration Award

Applicants for Enforcement: Bank of China, Bank of China Tokyo Branch, Sakura Bank (Japan), Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Hong Kong Branch (Japan), and Mitsui Trust Bank (Japan).

Party Subject to Enforcement: Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd.

The party subject to enforcement, Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd., is a legal person established as a joint venture between China Sports Service Company and Hong Kong Jiaxing (China) Investment Co., Ltd. For the construction of the Olympic Hotel, it entered into a loan agreement on March 20, 1987 with a consortium composed of the five applicant banks, namely Bank of China, Bank of China Tokyo Branch, Sakura Bank (Japan), Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Hong Kong Branch (Japan), and Mitsui Trust Bank (Japan), which provided that the five banks would extend a loan of 5 billion Japanese yen to Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd. A "mortgage agreement" was also entered into, stipulating that the Olympic Hotel would serve as collateral for the loan and that its provision was one of the prerequisites for the lending parties to grant the loan facility. The five banks, including Bank of China, fulfilled all disbursement obligations under the loan agreement, but Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd. failed to repay the principal and accrued interest on the loan when due. A dispute arose between the parties regarding the performance of the "mortgage agreement." As negotiations failed, the five banks, including Bank of China, applied for arbitration with the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission pursuant to the arbitration clause in the "mortgage agreement."

The China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission rendered the following award: 1. The "mortgage agreement" entered into on March 20, 1987 between the applicants, the five banks including Bank of China, and the respondent, Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd., is valid; 2. The applicants are entitled, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, to dispose of the security interests specified in the agreement and to apply the proceeds from such disposition to satisfy the amounts owed by the respondent to the applicants as of September 20, 1994, totaling approximately 5.718 billion Japanese yen, together with interest on the said amount from September 20, 1994 until the date of actual payment, calculated at the interest rate determined in the "loan agreement" entered into on March 20, 1987 between the applicants and the respondent; 3. The respondent shall pay the applicants' attorney fees and preservation fees totaling over RMB 329,900; 4. The arbitration fees of over USD 185,800 and over RMB 971,500 shall be borne by the respondent.

After the arbitration award became effective, since the party subject to enforcement, Olympic Hotel Co., Ltd., failed to comply with the award, the applicants for enforcement, the five banks including Bank of China, applied to the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court for enforcement pursuant to Article 217, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting the court to permit them to take over the Olympic Hotel and realize the "security interests" confirmed as valid by the arbitration award, so as to use the proceeds from the disposition of the "security interests" to satisfy the principal and interest owed by the party subject to enforcement.

Upon review, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held that the so-called "disposition of security interests" in the arbitration award meant the realization of the mortgage rights. Therefore, the content of enforcement should be to deliver all movable and immovable properties of the Olympic Hotel, which is the mortgaged property, to the applicants for enforcement. In order to avoid affecting the normal operation of the hotel during enforcement while smoothly completing the inventory and verification of the hotel's property and ensuring the handover of the hotel, the court decided to adopt the "trusteeship method" for enforcement. That is, it appointed Beijing Liuhexing Hotel Management Company to enter the Olympic Hotel, complete the verification of the hotel's assets within a specified period, and manage and operate the hotel on its behalf.

On November 18, 1998, based on the report of Liuhexing Hotel Management Company, the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court determined that the verification work had been completed and formally transferred all assets of the Olympic Hotel to the applicants for enforcement, the five banks including Bank of China. Thus, this enforcement case involving a substantial subject matter was concluded.
